svg.text: AeroBook Flight Platform — Data Flow Architecture
Gane & Sarson Standard • Microservice Transformation Nodes, Isolated Repositories & External Integrations • Black Canvas System Standard

g.text: • Validates seat availability lock with P3.0
• Inquires dynamic pricing quote with P4.0
• Checks flight departure window (T-24h to T-1h)
• Verifies PNR & passenger eligibility with D5
• Assigns seat, generates encrypted QR pass
• Verifies gate barcode scans for E3 gate staff
• Formats HTML flight itinerary & SMS payload

svg.text: Asynchronous Delivery: Email Ticket & SMS PNR Alert

g.text: AEROBOOK DATA FLOW GOVERNANCE & ARCHITECTURAL GUARANTEES
Each microservice encapsulates its own MySQL schema (aerobook_auth_db, aerobook_flight_db, etc.).
Direct foreign keys across databases are strictly prohibited; entity correlation occurs via immutable UUIDs and PNRs.
Prevents tight coupling, deadlock cascades, and allows independent scaling and horizontal database replication.
Zero plain-text credit card storage. Card tokens are authorized exclusively through third-party gateways (E4).
Booking saga coordinates two-phase seat lock verification before committing the reservation in aerobook_booking_db.
If payment fails or times out, the transient seat hold is immediately relinquished back into the flight inventory.
High-throughput, asynchronous decoupling via RabbitMQ message broker with guaranteed delivery.
Booking confirmation emails and SMS alerts are processed out-of-band by asynchronous notification consumers.
Dead-Letter Exchanges (DLX) and retry backoff policies ensure zero notification drop during high-load surges.
